title: stream-splitter batcher: introduce stage boundaries and compact KV frontier
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Our continuous-batcher has accumulated ad-hoc responsibilities (prefetch, admission, slot allocation, commit) and the KV cache interface is tightly coupled to the batcher internals. This makes small changes risky, increases contention under skewed workloads, and complicates kernel-selection experiments.

Goal: Decompose the continuous-batcher into clearly defined, testable stage boundaries (Ingress splitter, Admission gate, Slot allocator, Commit sink) and introduce a lightweight KV Frontier adapter that provides a small, stable subset of KV operations (lookup/prime/evict/compact) plus a frontier API for safe eviction and incremental compaction. The refactor should enable per-stage backpressure, finer-grained profiling, and eventual replacement of the scheduler with a per-shard actor runtime.

Non-goal: We are not rewriting the execution kernels or changing model semantics. This ticket focuses on structural cleanup, observable contracts, and the KV adapter surface (not full cache reimplementation).

Design links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1s-example-stream-splitter-design (design doc), https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/9153 (prototype PR), https://dashboards.redwood.ai/dashboard/continuous-batcher-tail-latency (dashboard).
acceptance_criteria: Batcher split into four explicit stages with documented interfaces: Ingress splitter, Admission gate, Slot allocator, Commit sink
KV Frontier adapter implemented with unit + integration tests and feature-flag behind runtime-1.22
End-to-end regression tests pass for existing workloads with no semantic changes
Quantified perf targets: 99th-percentile request latency reduced by >=12% under production trace replay and KV read amplification reduced by >=25% for hot-key skew tests
Observability: stage-level metrics and distributed tracing spans are emitted for each request path
Migration plan documented and migration tool included to convert in-flight slot leases to new allocator state
tasks: Create lightweight stage interfaces and move prefetch logic into Ingress splitter
Implement Admission gate with backpressure and admission metrics
Design and implement Slot allocator API and slot lease transition helper
Extract KV Frontier adapter and add compact/evict primitives
Wire stage-level tracing and expose metrics in Console (per-stage latency, queue depth)
Add integration tests using production trace replayer and compare tail latencies
Create migration utility to drain and convert existing slot leases
Code review, runtime canary rollout, and post-rollout latency analysis

2026-02-02 - Marco Chen: Drafted API for KV Frontier; kept operations minimal to avoid leaking cache internals. Shared prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/9153

2026-02-08 - Priya Rao (reviewer): Design looks good; two requests: (1) add explicit invariants for slot-lease handoff to avoid double-free on failure, (2) metric names should match Console conventions. Added as follow-up tasks.

2026-02-18 - Marco Chen: Posted benchmark results from staging replayer. Observed 14% reduction in 99th latency for small-sequence workloads, but large-sequence workloads show regression under extreme KV eviction pressure. Root cause traced to compaction triggering in the prototype.
2026-02-22 - Infrastructure team (note): Upgraded tokio to 1.31 in a separate dependency bump (ENG-38977) — confirmed compatibility with current branch, no ABI issues.
2026-02-28 - Marco Chen: Implemented incremental compaction in KV Frontier and added a fast-path for hot-key priming. Re-ran replayer: tail latencies within target and read amplification down 28%.
2026-03-04 - QA - L. Nguyen: Integration smoke passed against canary; added flaky test for slot handoff; filing follow-up (ENG-39245) to harden handoff under network partitions.

2026-03-10 - Marco Chen: Preparing canary rollout plan and playbook. Canary will start at 2 small Dedicated clusters with slow ramp and observability alarms for tail latency, error rate, and KV miss amplification.
notes: Follow-ups: (1) Replace global scheduler with per-shard actor model (tracked as separate epic), (2) Evaluate moving KV Frontier to a persistent index to reduce rebuild costs, (3) Post-mortem and perf blamemap after canary finishes.
